title: Wealthfolio
intro: A local-first app that tracks your investments and net worth, for people who don't want their money data sitting in someone else's cloud.
body: Monarch Money Core is $99.99 a year. Wealthfolio tracks your portfolio and spending on your own device, with no account and no cloud database. The README says manual tracking and CSV import are free forever. Automatic syncing with your brokerage needs Wealthfolio Connect, which is their own subscription and it's optional. So you type in your trades yourself or you end up paying for another plan anyway. 109 people have contributed and the last commit was today.
verdict: Run it next to Monarch for a month. If CSV imports are enough for your accounts, cancel the subscription.
other_side: Keep paying if you want your accounts to sync by themselves and don't want to add another subscription for it.

title: Twenty
intro: An open source CRM that technical teams build and change in code, made for people who are leaving Salesforce.
body: Salesforce Starter Suite costs $25 per user a month. Twenty is an open source CRM, and the README says it's for technical teams who define their objects and fields as code. There's a hosted cloud, or you can self-host and run the server yourself. 807 people have contributed and the last commit was today. The catch is that it's a CRM you build, so somebody on the team has to write that code.
verdict: Try Twenty next to Salesforce if there's a developer on the team who can set it up for the way you sell.
other_side: Keep paying if nobody on your team wants to set up a CRM and keep it running.

title: Firecrawl
intro: Open source scraper and search API that pulls web pages and gives back clean data an AI agent can use.
body: Firecrawl Cloud Hobby is $19 a month, or $16 a month if you pay for the year. The code is open source and you can host it yourself, and then it's your server and you keep it running. The README says it handles proxies and rate limits for you. It doesn't say how much of that still works when you host it yourself. It got 795 stars today. A normal day is about 215. The last commit was today.
verdict: If you already run servers, try it next to Firecrawl Cloud, and once it handles the sites you scrape you can cancel Firecrawl Cloud.
other_side: Keep paying if you don't want to run your own scraping server and fix it yourself.

title: It's a Plan
intro: A self-hosted issue tracker for teams that want AI agents and people picking up issues from the same board.
body: Linear Basic is $10 per user a month. For a team of ten that's $100. This one tracks issues and, according to the README, hands them to AI agents like they're teammates. It runs on your own server, and the built-in agents need your own API key. 56 people have worked on it and someone committed today. It's only 128 days old, and nobody picks up the phone when it breaks.
verdict: If your team already runs its own servers, try it next to Linear and only move over once it's held up for a few cycles.
other_side: Keep paying if nobody on your team wants to look after a server.

facts.description: ⭐️⭐️⭐️ Open-source, self-hosted alternative to Linear and Plane. Project management and issue tracking where teams and AI agents work side by side to plan and ship products.
facts.readme_excerpt: # The open-source Linear alternative where AI agents take issues like teammates Use it as a regular issue tracker from day one. When you are ready, give an agent an issue the way you give it to a colleague, and review the result yourself or let another agent check it. Put agents on a schedule, or build a workflow that passes an issue from agent to agent. Self-hosted, on your own server.         If It's a Plan looks useful to you, star the repo ⭐ and [leave a review on Product Hunt](https://www.producthunt.com/products/it-s-a-plan/reviews).                     ## Why It's a Plan - **Agents as project members.** Each gets a role, permissions and an assignee slot, and works on the same board as your people. - **Two kinds of agents.** Internal agents run on your server, on any model with your API key. External agents run on your machine through [`@itsaplan/runner`](packages/runner), under your own Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI or opencode account. - **Any kind of work.** Software, marketing, design, support, sales, operations, research. - **Yours to run.** Your server and your database. ## Community features | Area | What you get | | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Product management | Kanban, table, timeline, and calendar views · cycles · custom fields · dashboards · docs · notes boards · project templates · import from Linear, Trello, and Plane | | AI agents | Agents as project members · internal on any

title: AFFiNE
intro: An open-source workspace that keeps docs and whiteboards in one place, for people who'd otherwise use Notion and Miro.
body: Notion Plus is €9.50 per seat a month. AFFiNE you host yourself, so you run it and you fix it. The README says it's local-first and puts docs and whiteboard on one canvas. It has 276 contributors and the last commit was yesterday. It got 170 stars today, and a normal day brings about 48. The reason to stay on Notion is moving the whole team wiki over and then having nobody to call when it breaks.
verdict: Run AFFiNE next to Notion for a few weeks before you cancel any seats.
other_side: Keep paying if your team already lives in Notion and nobody wants to look after a server.
